facts.text: The city’s completed 2026 pool-renovation description lists zero-depth entry with handrails. It does not specify gradients or the connection from parking.
facts.quote: Zero Depth Entry - Easy, walk-in pool access with ADA-accessible handrails

facts.text: The separate family wading pool also has zero-depth entries. This does not establish transfer equipment or entry arrangements for every pool feature.
facts.quote: Zero-Depth Entries – Easy access for little swimmers and those with mobility needs.

facts.text: The 2026 renovation description lists shaded seating by the updated eating area, plus more shade on the deck and in the water. It does not identify reserved wheelchair or companion spaces.
facts.quote: Updated Eating Area - New service windows, fencing, and shaded seating area 7. Expanded Shade - Significant increase in both on-deck and in-water shade options

facts.text: The membership page lists family changing rooms, individual shower stalls in the locker rooms and a lounge. Adult changing equipment, transfer space and doorway details are not specified.
facts.quote: Locker Rooms with Dry Saunas & Individual Shower Stalls Family Changing Rooms Lounge Area

facts.text: Membership eligibility includes Blue Ash residents, full- or part-time employees of Blue Ash businesses, and full-time UC Blue Ash students. Annual verification is required; ask the Welcome Desk which documents apply to your category.
facts.quote: a valid driver's license and a current utility bill (last 30 days) or lease showing a Blue Ash mailing address Senior Citizen Memberships (50% off standard rates) Available to individuals 62 years or older and their spouses Family memberships may include spouse and dependent children (24 and under) living in the household Memberships for Individuals with Disabilities (50% off standard rates) Requires state verification of disability status If the head of household meets eligibility, their family membership is also discounted Business Memberships Open to full-time and part-time employees of Blue Ash-based businesses Must provide a valid driver's license and a recent pay stub showing Blue Ash City tax payment Family Memberships Includes: One individual and legally claimed dependents (24 and under) Married couples and their dependent children Elderly parents or adult children (25+) may be included if legally claimed as dependents UC Blue Ash Student Memberships Available to full-time UC Blue Ash students Annual verification required

facts.text: Memberships are purchased at the Recreation Center Welcome Desk. Application and waiver forms can be printed ahead or completed on site.
facts.quote: Where: Recreation Center Welcome Desk When: Monday-Friday: 6am-7pm Saturday, 8am-4pm Sunday, 10am-2pm What to bring: Full annual membership fee (paid at purchase or renewal) Proof of residency or employment in Blue Ash Residents: Driver's License or current Utility Bill Employment: Current Paystub showing Blue Ash taxes Membership Application Form Facility Waiver *To speed up the membership process, forms (found at top of page) can be printed, filled out, and brought with you - or completed on-site if needed.

facts.text: The city lists a 50% membership discount for individuals with disabilities, requiring state verification of disability status. A qualifying head of household can also receive the family-membership discount.
facts.quote: Memberships for Individuals with Disabilities (50% off standard rates) Requires state verification of disability status If the head of household meets eligibility, their family membership is also discounted

facts.text: The equipment page places the indoor track, two NuSteps and an upper-body ergometer on the fitness center’s second floor. It does not describe an elevator route or transfer assistance.
facts.quote: Fitness Center: Second Floor Indoor Track 1/10th mile around Punching bag located on one corner of the track Pull up bar located on one corner of the track 45+ Cardio Machines Precor AMTs (4) Precor Ellipticals (6) Precor Treadmills (12) Precor Recumbent Bikes (6) Precor Upright Bikes (3) Arc Trainers (4) Keiser Total Body Trainer Bikes (2) Keiser Cycling Bikes (3) Matrix Stair Climbers (2) Nusteps (2) Rowers (4) Matrix Upper Body Ergometer (1)

facts.text: Fitness orientations last 30–60 minutes, depend on staff availability and are arranged within two weeks of submitting the form. Ask about equipment and any support needed before attending.
facts.quote: Orientations are scheduled by the availability of our fitness staff. Sessions will be arranged within 2 weeks of form submission. Duration Each orientation lasts 30 to 60 minutes.

facts.text: The home page still carries a fitness-floor repair notice beginning September 28 and forecasting up to six weeks of work, with the center open but its layout and space affected. The notice does not confirm completion; check current conditions before travelling.
facts.quote: Portions of the Fitness Center floor will be closed for repairs beginning September 28. Repairs are expected to take up to six weeks. The Fitness Center will remain open, but the layout and available space will be temporarily impacted.

facts.text: The published outdoor-pool schedule is for 2026 and includes Labor Day weekend, September 5–7. It does not establish November swimming or a 2027 season.
facts.quote: Labor Day Weekend - September 5, 6, and 7

facts.text: The plunge and competitive pools have in-deck lifts, while the family play pool has zero-depth entry. The city asks visitors to have a caregiver available to help with equipment if necessary. Confirm lift availability before visiting.
facts.quote: The family play pool is designed for zero depth entrance. Additionally, the plunge and competitive pools have an in-deck lift system for easy pool entry. Please have a caregiver available to assist you with the equipment if necessary.

facts.text: The linked facility guide, revised April 2026, says staff demonstrate equipment but are not permitted to lift people. Have a caregiver available if assistance is needed; the guide does not establish a lift model or weight limit.
facts.quote: Please have a caregiver available to assist if necessary. Staff are not permitted to lift people but will demonstrate how to operate equipment.

facts.text: The pool house has men’s and women’s locker rooms and a family restroom. The page does not describe toilet transfer space, door controls or adult changing equipment.
facts.quote: The pool house has both men's and women's locker rooms, a family restroom, and a concession stand.

facts.text: The Aquatic Center requires membership or entry as a current member’s guest; single-day pool passes are not offered. Confirm arrangements for a caregiver when planning a visit.
facts.quote: The Aquatic Center is a membership-based facility, you must have a membership or be a guest of a current member to enter. Single day pool passes are not offered.

facts.text: Resident, business and non-resident memberships are offered. Membership must be bought in person at the Community Center front desk; online purchase is unavailable. Registration hours differ from general facility hours.
facts.quote: includes a resident pass, business pass, and a non-resident pass. There are three tiers to the pass system: Tier 1 is a single-person household. Tier 2 is a two-person household. Tier 3 is a household of up to five members. Any household with more than five members will be charged an additional $10 per person. Two forms of proof of residency and/or proof of working within the Sharonville city limits will be required to be eligible for a Resident or Business pass. Membership Registration Hours Memberships must be purchased in person at the Community Center front desk. They are NOT available for purchase online.

facts.text: The pool’s guest rules require guests over 18 to provide a driver’s licence or state ID for the SafePoint scan. Guests sign in and must leave with their member. The page does not state a caregiver exception.
facts.quote: All guests over the age of 18 are required to provide a valid Driver's License or State ID to be scanned by our SafePoint system against the National Sex Offenders Registry. Members are responsible for the behavior of their guests while they are in our facility. The Recreation Department reserves the right to ban future entry. All guests are required to complete the guest sign in sheet when entering the Community Center. Guests are required to leave the facility with the member once they have completed their activity/concluded their visit.

facts.text: Water bottles are allowed around the pool; other food and drink are prohibited under the posted rules. Medical-food exceptions are not described, so discuss any needs before visiting.
facts.quote: With the exception of water bottles, food and drink of any kind are not permitted around the pool area.

facts.text: Baby changing stations are inside the locker rooms, and changing diapers in the pool area is prohibited. A baby changing station does not establish an adult changing facility.
facts.quote: Baby changing stations are located inside the locker rooms. Board of Health restrictions requires that you do not change diapers in the pool area.

facts.text: For information or support concerning program and facility access, the April 2026 facility guide directs visitors to 513-563-2895. A request does not confirm a particular accommodation.
facts.quote: If you are a person with a special need and would like more information and/or support for accessibility of programs and facilities, please contact us at 513-563-2895.

facts.text: The Community Center lists a banked indoor walking/running track of one-twelfth mile. The listing does not describe an elevator connection, track slope or usable width.
facts.quote: Indoor Track - 1/12 mile banked running/walking track

facts.text: The Summer 2026 Hometown Guide lists September 7 as the pool’s final day. This is a past seasonal schedule, not November operation or a 2027 opening date.
facts.quote: September 7th - final day.

facts.text: Guided store tours require advance reservations, run on weekdays and last about an hour. Tours can be tailored to special requirements for groups of eight or more; smaller groups can often be paired with others. Confirm arrangements rather than assuming a private or quieter tour.
facts.quote: Guided tours are offered weekdays by appointment only, subject to availability. Tours can be tailored to meet special requirements, interests, and to fit groups of 8 or more (smaller groups can often be paired with others). Comfortable shoes are suggested, as a good deal of walking is involved. We invite you to take a tour of the store and enjoy food samples from around the world! $5.00/Person Available Monday-Friday Store Tours last approximately one hour What's Included? • Tasty food samples as you tour the store. • $2.00 Jungle Jim's International Market Gift Certificates. • Tour Guide w/ microphone.

facts.text: The guided store tour includes a guide with a microphone and food samples. This does not establish hearing-loop support, captions or an allergy-free experience.
facts.quote: Tasty food samples as you tour the store. • $2.00 Jungle Jim’s International Market Gift Certificates. • Tour Guide w/ microphone.

facts.text: Tour availability is limited during holidays and December. Fairfield tour reservations use 513-674-6023 or tours-ff@junglejims.com.
facts.quote: Limited tour availability during holidays and the month of December. • Summer camp tours are offered (schedule in advance). • Adult Team-Building Scavenger Hunts available. • Tour buses are always welcome. • Tour dates and times are subject to availability. Fairfield Reservations tours-ff@junglejims.com 513-674-6023

facts.text: The visit page offers a printable Fairfield store map alongside the app map. The linked file’s URL says June 2021, but the PDF title says August 2026 and its printed copyright says 2026. It is a diagram, not a current route photograph.
facts.quote: Store Map Your personal guide to the World of Food. Fairfield Eastgate

facts.text: Rowe Visitor Center offers places to relax in the Whittaker Library and near wildlife-observation windows. The page does not designate these as quiet rooms or describe seating layouts.
facts.quote: Relax in the Whittaker Library or near the wildlife observation windows.

facts.text: Uncovered picnic tables are outside the Nature PlayScape near Krehbiel Pavilion and at the base of the Rowe Visitor Center parking lot. Picnic areas are first come, first served; table clearances and route surfaces are not specified.
facts.quote: Cincinnati Nature Center offers two areas to picnic on a first-come, first-served basis. There are uncovered picnic tables outside the Nature PlayScape, near the Krehbiel Pavilion, and at the base of Rowe Visitor Center parking lot.

facts.text: For program-access questions or support, contact the front desk at 513-831-1711 or cnc@cincynature.org before registering. This is an advance-discussion process, not confirmation that every program can provide every accommodation.
facts.quote: If you have an accessibility question or need, please feel free to reach out to our front desk staff at (513) 831-1711 or contact cnc@cincynature.org before registering.

facts.text: Admission ends 20 minutes before closing, hiking after hours is prohibited and trails may close in severe weather. Confirm the day’s grounds hours; the visit page mixes a June heading with a November seasonal section.
facts.quote: Admission ends 20 minutes prior to closing. For your safety, we do not allow hiking after hours, and we may close trails due to severe weather conditions.
Explore a variety of beautiful habitats, shaded areas, and interactive displays along our 0.72-mile, all-accessible Mashburn Family Discovery Trail.
facts.text: The center describes the 0.72-mile Mashburn Family Discovery Trail as all-accessible.

facts.quote: Both the Rowe Visitor Center, Krippendorf Lodge, and Nature PlayScape parking lots have designated ADA parking spaces.
facts.text: Designated accessible parking is listed at the Rowe Visitor Center, Krippendorf Lodge and Nature PlayScape lots.

facts.quote: Our trails at Rowe Woods vary from smooth, accessible boardwalks over ponds and walkways made of finely crushed limestone to natural, sloping trails with gravel or mulch surfaces. On trails farther out from the parking areas, you'll find rocky creek crossings and a handful of areas with steep stairs or inclines. Please stop by Rowe Visitor Center to connect with our Visitor Services team, or call (513) 831-1711 , to learn about our programs, building spaces, or trails. We would love to discuss your needs and provide accommodations and suggestions for a fantastic visit!
facts.text: Other trails vary in surface and slope, with some rocky creek crossings, steep stairs or inclines. Visitor Services can discuss routes and accommodation needs.

facts.quote: Our trails at Rowe Woods vary from smooth, accessible boardwalks over ponds and walkways made of finely crushed limestone to natural, sloping trails with gravel or mulch surfaces.
facts.text: Some routes use smooth, accessible boardwalks over ponds and walkways of finely crushed limestone.

facts.quote: An easy trail: • Is relatively flat • Is less than 1.25 miles in length • Is at least 3 feet in width • Has stream crossings with bridges
facts.text: The center rates a trail easy when it is relatively flat, under 1.25 miles, at least 3 feet wide, with bridged stream crossings.

facts.quote: Visitor restroom facilities are located behind Krehbiel Pavilion -just across from the Nature PlayScape and adjacent parking lot. This restroom also offers a shower station that is available to use after play sessions in the Mud Zone. ‍ Restrooms are also located inside Rowe Visitor Center. All restrooms are accessible during grounds hours, even if Rowe Visitor Center is closed. Water fountains and fountains for dogs are located near both restrooms.
facts.text: Restrooms are behind Krehbiel Pavilion and inside Rowe Visitor Center, with water fountains near both; the center says all restrooms are open during grounds hours even if the visitor center is closed.

facts.quote: This first-in-the-region Forest Ear-nocular is designed to amplify the subtle sounds of nature-birds calling, leaves rustling, streams flowing.
facts.text: The Forest Ear-nocular is designed to amplify the subtle sounds of nature.

facts.quote: You can purchase your tickets via credit or debit card and by showing your photo ID for your protection when you come to the gate. We do not accept cash payments for admission at the gatehouse.
facts.text: For non-member admission, the gatehouse accepts credit or debit cards and asks for photo ID; cash is not accepted. The mobile guide opens through a web link, with no download or password.

additionalSupport.quote: You can access the Mobile Guide by using this web link: https://bycell.mobi/CNCGuide . No downloads or passwords needed!

facts.quote: Motorized shopping carts and traditional wheelchairs are available at the main entrances at both locations.
facts.text: Motorized shopping carts and standard wheelchairs are available at the main entrances.

facts.quote: A Caroline Cart is available by special request at Customer Service.
facts.text: A Caroline Cart is available by special request at Customer Service.

facts.quote: Download the app for the ultimate Jungle Jim’s experience. Explore the jungle on an interactive store map, unlock exclusive in-app deals, and more!
facts.text: The Jungle Jim's app has an interactive store map.

facts.quote: We are not offering online ordering, pick up, or delivery for our regular in-store merchandise at this time.
facts.text: Regular in-store groceries cannot be ordered online for pickup or delivery, so shopping is in person.

facts.quote: No pets – service animals only.
facts.text: Pets are not allowed; the store’s policy permits service animals.

facts.quote: Setting foot on our Fairfield property, be prepared to explore a massive, zany maze of departments. You, your family, and friends will encounter some of our most classic attractions, animatronics, and even our elevated monorail gliding about the property during special events.
facts.text: The Fairfield description warns of a maze of departments and lists animatronics among its attractions. It does not describe quiet hours or a quiet route.

The April 2026 facility guide applies the guest ID requirement to ages 18 and older; the pool-rules webpage says over 18. Confirm the requirement for an 18-year-old guest and any caregiver arrangements.
facts.quote: ALL resident and non- resident guests, ages 18 years and older, purchasing a guest pass will be required to provide a valid driver's license or State ID Card.

additionalSupport.quote: All guests over the age of 18 are required to provide a valid Driver's License or State ID

facts.text: The center places Abner Hollow Pioneer Cabin on the Mashburn Family Discovery Trail near Witt Pollinator Garden and Matt’s Pond. The trail’s all-accessible label does not establish entry into the cabin or an uninterrupted interior route.
facts.quote: Stop by and explore Abner Hollow Pioneer Cabin via the all-accessible, 0.72-mile Mashburn Family Discovery Trail, near Witt Pollinator Garden and Matt's Pond.

facts.text: For Light in the Forest’s 2026 season, the FAQ describes an approximately one-mile, mostly flat trail with a slight incline, uneven areas and no paved surface. The operator says access requires help; confirm the assistance and surface conditions you need.
facts.quote: Our trail this year is about a mile and mostly flat. Is the trail handicap accessible? It is with help, as there is a slight incline and the trail is not 100% even. It is not a paved surface.

facts.text: For the 2026 Light in the Forest event, parking attendants guide visitors onto a circular, two-way trail rather than a single fixed starting point. This does not establish a measured parking-to-trail connection.
facts.quote: No, you'll be guided onto the trails by a parking attendant. No matter where you park, you'll be near the trail and can get on. The event route is a circular, two-way path.

facts.text: The 2026 Light in the Forest route is mostly outdoors and loops around Abner Hollow Cabin, through Rowe Visitor Center and Krippendorf Lodge for warming up. These stops are not confirmed quiet rooms; the event page also warns that trails can be muddy.
facts.quote: Most of the trail is outside. It loops around Abner Hollow Cabin, through Rowe Visitor Center and Krippendorf Lodge where you can warm up a bit.

additionalSupport.quote: The trails can be muddy, so wear appropriate footwear/boots.
The 2026 event is generously sponsored by:

facts.text: The restaurant has dining rooms upstairs and downstairs and no elevator. Confirm a first-floor table before booking; the page does not identify the step-free visitor doorway.
facts.quote: Please keep in mind that our historic building has dining rooms both upstairs and downstairs. We do not have an elevator.

facts.text: To request a first-floor table, the venue asks you to add a note under “Guests Notes” in its OpenTable booking or call the restaurant. A request is not confirmation of a table, entrance route or particular seating arrangement.
facts.quote: If you need to reserve a table on the first floor with full handicap accessibility, please make a note of it under “Guests Notes” on Open Table or give us a call.

facts.text: For reservations of more than ten people, the restaurant asks you to call 859-586-9900. Confirm the dining floor and companion/table arrangement directly when planning a group visit.
facts.quote: For reservations of over 10 people please call the restaurant at: 859-586-9900.
